subject: industrial-engineering
intro: Industrial engineering turns systems thinking into salaries: the people who make factories, hospitals and supply chains faster, safer and cheaper get paid to find the wasted seconds.

roles.title: Industrial Engineers
roles.what: Design, develop, test and evaluate integrated systems for managing industrial production processes, spanning quality control, inventory control, logistics and material flow, cost analysis, production coordination and the human factors of work.
roles.where: The whole syllabus is the job description: statistical process control and acceptance sampling from the quality unit, optimisation models, facility layout and line balancing, and production planning with MRP and JIT.

roles.title: Operations Research Analysts
roles.what: Formulate and apply mathematical modelling and optimising methods that help management make decisions, building decision-support software and supplying optimal time, cost or logistics networks for programs and operations.
roles.where: The operations research and optimisation unit is the core toolkit — linear programming, integer and network models, dynamic programming — and the simulation unit's discrete-event models and queuing theory extend it.

roles.title: Logisticians
roles.what: Analyse and coordinate a firm's ongoing logistical functions across the entire life cycle of a product, from acquisition, distribution and internal allocation to delivery and final disposal of resources.
roles.where: The production planning and inventory unit — forecasting and scheduling, MRP and JIT, supply chain coordination — plus facility location models from the facilities unit give you the vocabulary and methods logistics teams run on.

roles.title: Human Factors Engineers and Ergonomists
roles.what: Design objects, facilities and environments that optimise human well-being and overall system performance, investigating and analysing how human behaviour and performance interact with the technology people use.
roles.where: The work design and human factors unit is direct preparation: time and motion study, ergonomics and cognitive workload are the field's founding measurements, and the quality unit's data discipline backs the analysis.

roles.title: Industrial Production Managers
roles.entry: Bachelor's degree plus years of experience
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate the work activities and resources needed to manufacture products in accordance with cost, quality and quantity specifications, usually after climbing through production roles.
roles.where: Quality unit control charts become the dashboards you run a plant by, the production planning unit's MRP and JIT thinking drives daily scheduling, and simulation know-how helps you test changes before committing lines.
